    External MCP Server Catalog - Sweep Log, October 16-31, 2026¶

    Archive for October 16-31, 2026. Discovery passes appear newest first. The current sweep log carries the most recent passes.

    Archive: October 1-15, 2026 | November 1-15, 2026

    🆕 October 31, 2026 - Night Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)¶

    Four hours after the afternoon pass, and the movement came from the submission window rather than the directories: eighteen submissions landed on chatmcp/mcpso between #6513 at 19:06Z and #6530 at 03:53Z, while mcpservers.org carried no delta and the mcp.so recentServers block put exactly six cards above the afternoon stamp. Three shipped, and two of the three answered a live endpoint with no credential at all.

    • Lazynext Accessibility Checker MCP - WCAG Audits From Chat - remote Streamable HTTP at https://checker.lazynext.com/mcp, keyless, initialize answering HTTP 200 in 0.19 seconds with serverInfo accessibility-checker at 1.0.0 and tools/list returning all four tools with schemas, so the surface is measured rather than quoted. list_rules returned 75 WCAG criteria each tagged static or rendered, and two rendered scans were run on our own homepage. Mobile viewport: score 46 on score_model weighted-v1, 28 issues across 12 distinct criteria, section 508 conforms: false against the stated basis of WCAG 2.0 AA incorporated by 36 CFR 1194 E205.4 with 5 clauses implicated (302.1, 302.2, 302.3, 302.7, 302.9), a benchmark at the 54th percentile of 26 sites, and a persisted report at checker.lazynext.com/report/c036dcc1-4e6. Desktop viewport: the first call exceeded a 60-second client timeout and the retry returned in 61.1 seconds with score 46 and 29 issues. The findings are content-level and fixable: two wcag-2.5.3 failures where an aria-label replaces rather than contains the visible text, one wcag-1.4.10 on a <div> with a fixed 1000px width, and seven wcag-1.1.1 findings that are filename alt text. The reason it earns a guide is that this catalogue had no accessibility entry at all, which makes it the only tool here that answers a procurement questionnaire rather than a ranking question. Gap recorded: the vendor site lists API, MCP and A2A as Pro features at $9 per month with the free tier at 3 rendered scans a day, and yet the endpoint accepted no key and labelled both scans plan: "free", so the plan gate is documented and not enforced on the MCP path; scan_html, get_report and the site crawl were not exercised, the benchmark cohort of 26 or 27 sites is unpublished, and the repository is source available rather than open source.
    • distribution.tech MCP - Book X Creator Posts From the Chat - remote Streamable HTTP with a keyless guest tier at https://app.distribution.tech/api/mcp/guest: initialize HTTP 200 in 0.34 seconds, serverInfo distribution at 1.37.0, and six tools with full schemas. guest_status states its own limits, 60 calls per 10 minutes per client address and 3 plan_quote_guest calls per 7 days, and inventory at 04:02:35Z reported 1,005 approved X creators, 86 bookable now and 255 posts carrying a current price. resolve_audience on a described profile (a B2B AI data layer, ecommerce and SaaS operators, US) resolved three segments and narrowed the market to 792 creators, 63 bookable and 187 priced posts with thin: false, and that 213-creator gap between the network and one audience is the number a founder cannot get from a DM. The account surface is documented at /docs/agents as 22 tools and the design is the reason for the guide: a key carries a spend mandate, signing a plan produces a payment link inside that mandate, brands are reviewed before their agent can buy, creator names and two alternates arrive before signing, placements can be swapped before signing, and evidence returns per placement. Gap recorded: plan_quote_guest failed with unavailable: The network could not be read just now. Try again. and consumed one of the three weekly guest quotes, so no all-in price was obtained; no brand approval was sought and nothing was purchased, so create_campaign, approve_plan, evidence and the mandate enforcement are read rather than driven, and the creator payout split was not read.
    • GWIX MCP - Pay, Hiring and Workforce Data With Provenance - remote Streamable HTTP at https://api.gwix.ai/mcp, where the live server answered a keyless initialize with HTTP 401, JSON-RPC -32001, Authentication required: sign in with OAuth or send a GWIX API key as a Bearer token, and /v1/mcp returned a different 401 shape, an RFC 7807 problem body with a request_id, so the public API and the MCP server sit on different routers and both are closed. The vendor's keyless sample at https://api.gwix.ai/mcp/sample is where this pass measured: initialize HTTP 200, tools/list returning 27 tools in 37,580 bytes, and get_data_status for the US reporting release: "2026-W41", last_complete_week: "2026-04-12" and a sample covering the US, UK and Germany at 6 months of lag with history from 2024-10-14, market level only. get_pay for SOC 47-2111 in metro mtr_midland_tx for 2026-Q1, the exact example the vendor publishes, returned 74 ads with pay and percentiles of 38,215 / 48,368 / 66,781 / 76,526 / 94,694 USD per year, reproducing the vendor's own published median to the dollar, which is a stronger trust signal than any marketing page. The metadata carries the machinery: 13-week quarters of whole Monday to Sunday weeks, each country's currency converted at the period average with fx_rate per row, and occupation codes crosswalked to US SOC 2018 with each SOC held as a separate row set and never pooled. The slice is new here: the hiring entries in this catalogue are job boards and recruiting pipelines, and none of them returns pay percentiles from official surveys beside job-ad medians, which is the gap that decides an offer. Gap recorded: job_offer_check, the tool closest to a decision, returned a CloudFront 504 after 30.07 seconds while the row tools answered in 0.26 seconds, so the written-analysis path is unverified; no credential exists, so the report tools, get_account_usage and the credit accounting were not driven; the 247-country claim is the vendor's where the sample proves three; and the credit cost of a typical question could not be produced.

    Read and held. mcpservers.org /all came back with 23 unique slugs and the counter at 18,577 against 18,402 at the afternoon read, and every slug matched an existing file in the tree, so the page carried no delta and the counter moved because the catalogue grows rather than because the newest page changed. The six mcp.so cards above the afternoon stamp are dispositioned as follows, so the next pass cannot read them as fresh: corridome (2026-11-01T00:15:52Z) is a US private-equity and M&A register requiring its own membership, corridome.com answering 200 with no keyless surface, held on access in a class the filings entries already cover; browse-bridge (23:07:27Z) shares selected Chrome tabs with an agent at https://mcp.browsebridge.com, held in the deepest automation slice here; listing-698e96 (19:17:31Z) is Tabulya, a Russian-language spreadsheet with AI, Python and SQL, held as localised product; coinvello (19:10:08Z) is the same arrival as #6513 below; and myimage2life-8891ac (18:02:28Z) turns a chat image into a printed product, held as consumer retail. The eighteen submissions between #6513 and #6530 were read with bodies: Clearcote MCP (#6515) is the strongest hold of the window, about 20 tools on a Chromium fork whose fingerprint is set in C++ and whose get_cdp_endpoint hands the same browser to Playwright, Puppeteer, browser-use or Crawl4AI, held on class with the CDP handoff recorded as the feature to test; conductor (#6519) is 23 tools each carrying a mandatory verifier that checks the result in code before the client sees it, the most interesting reliability entry of the window and developer tooling; SKV (#6526) answered a keyless initialize at https://skv.network/mcp with serverInfo skv-memory 1.30.0 and more than 20 tools including a per-turn turn(user_message, draft) duty, a paged constitution, a shared cube library with voting, a court for version disputes and an isolated sandbox, held for one pass because memory plus governance is rarer than plain memory and the promotion test is whether the seal and the court are enforceable rather than self-reported; CSI MCP (#6517) drives SAP2000 and ETABS on Windows only with 67 of 67 rebuilt verification examples matching published values, held on platform and vertical; NexusBro (#6528) answered keyless at https://nexusbro.com/api/agents/mcp with two tools and a free five-page audit, held on saturation against eight SEO audit entries; Shipvo (#6527) answered at https://sim.shipvo.dev/mcp with serverInfo shipvo 0.0.6 and needs a key for its 18 tools, developer mobile testing; Frank (#6524) returned a measured 401 at https://api.hifrank.ai/mcp on 14 tools of AI-moderated customer interviews, held on saturation against four research entries with the quotable-evidence question recorded; CoinVello (#6513), ILens (#6514), Fittest (#6516), recall (#6518), Betterloop (#6520), Wordy Page (#6521), nana800 (#6522), ytranscript (#6525) and VocaLingo (#6530) round out the window in the agent payments, developer tooling, materials science, memory, analytics, publishing, locale, transcript and media generation classes this catalogue already carries.

    Count. The guide tree held 1,073 server entries before this pass and holds 1,076 after it, across 1,466 files. Sources: the mcp.so homepage recentServers block read directly (132 parsed cards, newest 2026-11-01T00:15:52Z), mcpservers.org /all through the r.jina.ai reader proxy with X-Return-Format: html (23 unique slugs, counter 18,577), the chatmcp/mcpso issue window #6513 to #6530 read with bodies, a keyless initialize, tools/list, list_rules and two rendered scan_url calls on https://checker.lazynext.com/mcp (200, 4 tools, 75 rules, 12.97s mobile and 61.1s desktop), a keyless initialize, tools/list, guest_status, inventory, resolve_audience and one failed plan_quote_guest on https://app.distribution.tech/api/mcp/guest (200, 6 tools), a keyless initialize on https://api.gwix.ai/mcp (401) and on /v1/mcp (401), a keyless initialize, tools/list, get_data_status and get_pay on https://api.gwix.ai/mcp/sample (200, 27 tools) with one job_offer_check failing at a CloudFront 504, a keyless initialize on https://skv.network/mcp and https://sim.shipvo.dev/mcp (200), a keyless initialize and tools/list on https://nexusbro.com/api/agents/mcp (200, 2 tools), a measured 401 on https://api.hifrank.ai/mcp, and HTTP reads on gwix.ai, gwix.ai/mcp, gwix.ai/pricing, corridome.com, coinvello.com/ai, checker.lazynext.com, distribution.tech, distribution.tech/docs, distribution.tech/docs/agents and distribution.tech/pricing, all 200.

    🆕 October 31, 2026 - Afternoon Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)¶

    Two and a half hours after the midday pass, and the arrivals came from three different surfaces rather than one: a single new card on the mcp.so recentServers block above the 14:37:33Z stamp, two submission issues that landed after the midday window closed, and an mcpservers.org page that carried no delta at all. All three that shipped answered a live endpoint on the first request, which is the rule this pass applies before anything gets a guide.

    • HandbookHub MCP - Employee Handbooks in Chat - remote Streamable HTTP at https://api.handbookhub.com/mcp, a keyless initialize answering HTTP 401 in 0.37 seconds with A valid API token is required and an invalid_token code plus a requestId, which is the normal state for a connector bound to a workspace. Four read-only tools, documented in full on the vendor's own MCP page: list_handbooks with cursor paging and a limit of 100, get_handbook for metadata and the nested page structure, get_page for the latest saved page as plain text with its source URL, and search_handbooks at 20 searches per minute and 1,000 per day per organization across keyword, title and semantic matching, returning a score, a snippet and a URL per hit with no AI answer generated.     • kosa8 MCP - Sealed microVMs You Can Rewind · a local stdio gateway plus a Claude Code plugin, card filed on mcp.so 2026-10-31 at 03:22:19Z, verified and featured, kosa8.com, kosa8.com/pricing/ and kosa8.com/download/ all 200, github.com/kosa8ai/kosa8-claude-plugin 200 and MIT, documentation live at docs.kosa8.com at release v0.11.0. The pitch is one machine per tool server: kosa8 mcp add takes an image, an egress allow-list and the tool names you permit, and each registered server then runs as a container in a sandbox named mcp-NAME with its own network rule, no visibility of the other servers and none of your files, against the usual npx launch that runs somebody else's program as you with your keys. Tools are namespaced to NAME_tool, their descriptions prefixed with where they run and marked potentially destructive so clients that ask before destructive calls will ask, and a name collision is skipped rather than allowed to shadow. The pin is the part worth the entry. Every permission model built for MCP so far watches the tool name, the argument schema or the server identity, and all three stay constant while the thing the model actually reads changes: a tool description is prose, a model follows prose, and a server that edits its description has changed what your assistant will do without touching a field any permission list can see. kosa8 pins each definition on first use and withholds a later change until a person approves it, which turns the description from mutable copy into evidence. Around that, thirty built-in tools, checkpoint at about 0.7 seconds and rewind at about one for the whole running machine with memory and processes included, fork into live copies, an egress broker that injects API keys on the way out so the sandbox holds only a placeholder, approvals requiring one or two named people, and a hash-chained audit log. Gap recorded: nothing was installed or executed, so the thirty tools and the 213 documented commands are the vendor's publications, the card's documentation link points at kosa8.com/docs which answers 404, and the MIT licence covers the plugin rather than the signed daemon that runs the VMs.

    • Spark Inventory MCP - Stock, Forecasts and Draft POs · remote Streamable HTTP at https://api.sparkinventory.com/mcp, a keyless tools/list answering HTTP 401 Unauthorized in 0.4 seconds, the normal state for a connector bound to a vendor account. Card filed on mcp.so 2026-10-30 at 22:19:40Z, verified and featured, transport Streamable HTTP, authType oauth, category Productivity, no public repository because the service is closed. The audience is named precisely, which is rarer than it should be: product brands, wholesalers and 3PLs. Four directions are described, stock and risk by SKU, location and warehouse with on hand, incoming, days of supply and stockout risk; Demand ESP forecasts; reorder recommendations sized to lead time and MOQ with draft purchase orders; and operations reads and writes across sales orders, suppliers, transfers, receiving, pick lists and reports. Two sentences carry the design and they are the reason this is a new slice rather than a stock ledger: the forecasting model is picked per SKU by backtest, and the history is corrected for stockouts. The second one is where most implementations quietly fail, because a SKU that sold out in week three records low sales for the rest of the month, an uncorrected model reads the hole as falling demand, forecasts less, reorders less, and the next stockout is caused by the tool that was meant to prevent it. A confidence level per forecast is the difference between an answer and a number. Two containment statements are on the card, governed writes that you review and approve and purchase orders drafted rather than issued, which keeps the irreversible step in human hands while the agent assembles the join an operator cannot do by hand: current stock, open POs, supplier lead times and the forecast live in four places. The vendor also runs an SMS assistant, Sparki, and states that Spark Inventory is an official app inside ChatGPT, with a Claude connector coming soon and therefore not one-click today. Gap recorded: tools/list needs a token, so the tool names, count and write surface are the vendor's published position and not a list this pass measured, and a trial should settle whether forecast confidence comes back as a quotable field, whether a draft PO can land in an existing ERP, and what the connectors actually cover for Shopify or a 3PL.
    • offprompt MCP - API Keys That Never Enter the Chat · local stdio over npm at 0.3.0, MIT, npx offprompt init registering the server for the agents it detects, Node 22 or later, and the npm record carrying zero runtime dependencies and one bin entry, which for a tool whose job is handling secrets is the cheapest supply-chain check available and a real one. The inversion is the point: when an agent needs a credential it calls collect_secret, a page opens on 127.0.0.1, the value is typed by a person, and it is written straight into .env.local or a named file, so the agent receives the key's name and a fingerprint and never the value. Two more tools complete the surface, await_secret for the case where the agent must wait for the human step rather than race past it, and cancel_secret, the abort path a two-tool design usually forgets. 65 provider formats are checked as the value is typed, which catches the two mistakes that actually happen, the wrong key copied from a dashboard holding three of them and a truncated paste, and catches them at the page rather than at a 401 an hour later where the agent reports the wrong cause. The fingerprint is the design decision worth copying: a tool that returns only "ok" leaves the agent unable to tell a key it just collected from one already in the file, which is exactly how a production key ends up in a staging test. The distinction from the catalogue's Vaultwarden MCP is intake versus retrieval, a new key entering a working tree versus a stored password being read back, and the trade to make deliberately is the cloud-sandbox path, where a Cloudflare quick tunnel exposes the page because 127.0.0.1 inside a container is not your laptop. Gap recorded: nothing was installed or executed, the three tool names are the vendor's publication, and whether the file write accepts any path the agent names, whether await_secret blocks or polls, and whether the tunnel is scoped to one collection are all one install away from being answered.

    🆕 October 30, 2026 - Late Morning Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)¶

    Fifty-five minutes after the midday pass, and a short window earns its keep by testing the opposite thing: almost nothing can have changed, so what did change sits at the top of the newest page where you can see it. That is also the window that catches duplicates before they are written twice, and this pass caught two.

    • Tuqui MCP - Odoo in Chat, Read-Only by Default · remote Streamable HTTP at https://tuqui.com/mcp, answering a keyless tools/list with HTTP 401 {"error":"unauthorized"}, which is the expected state for a connector bound to a vendor account rather than an API key. The card was filed on mcp.so on 2026-10-21 and carries repository github.com/Tuqui-AI/tuqui-mcp (HTTP 200), docs at docs.tuqui.com (HTTP 200) and LGPL-3.0. The claim is the absence of a build: nothing installed in Odoo, no module deployed, one URL added to the assistant. Two sentences carry the security review, read-only by default and only what your Odoo user can see, and the second is the design decision that makes it deployable at all, because Odoo already maintains per-user record rules for multi-company and per-warehouse access, so binding the connector to an Odoo user reuses the model the business already runs instead of inventing a parallel one. Versions 16 through 20 across Community, Enterprise, Odoo Online, Odoo.sh and self-hosted. The comparison that matters is against the Odoo server this catalogue already carries, and it is not setup versus no setup because both claim little Odoo-side configuration: the split is that the local server takes ODOO_DB and ODOO_PASSWORD into your own config while this one holds the session vendor-side behind a consent screen, and that the local server is generic by design (query any model, filter by domain) while this one puts a skills layer for sales, stock and collections in front of the ORM. Gap recorded: tools/list needs a token, so the tool count and the write behaviour are the vendor's published position and not a list this pass drove.
    • MarketPrint MCP - Print on Demand to Your Store · remote Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.marketprint.de/mcp, answering HTTP 401 with Missing bearer token. Connect via OAuth, or use a static mcpacct_ token from your account settings. That refusal is better than most because it names both credential paths, which is the difference between an agent that reports a bare failure and one that knows what to try next. Card filed 2026-10-14, vendor MarketConsultive GmbH, authType oauth, no repository because the service is closed. Production is split by destination, Germany for Europe and Houston, Texas for the USA, which in print-on-demand is not a footnote but the difference between a shipping estimate that survives a customs form and one that does not, and it means the destination belongs in the conversation as a real field rather than an inference. Four channels: Shopify, Etsy, WooCommerce and TikTok Shop, which are four different commercial models wearing the same word "listing". This is the catalogue's first print-on-demand entry and its first look at the supply side, where a physical object begins to exist, rather than a fifth opinion on storefront health, and the failure mode is correspondingly worse: a bad read costs a wrong answer, a bad publish costs a live listing with a wrong price attached to a product that will actually be manufactured. Gap recorded: the publish path is capable but unverified, and a trial should settle draft-versus-live publishing, per-channel pricing and whether listings read back for reconciliation.
    • Casus MCP - French Tax and Legal Corpus in Chat · remote Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.wearecasus.com/mcp, answering HTTP 401 to a keyless tools/list and HTTP 405 to a bare GET, the normal pair for an OAuth-gated endpoint that speaks only POST. Flagged official on mcpservers.org at position 2 of the newest page. The corpus is deliberately national rather than broad: 230,419 articles of 77 codes from Légifrance with their successive versions, the BOFiP administrative doctrine, more than 3.4 million court decisions searchable by number or ECLI, tax treaties and EU law, as of 18 October 2026. The reason to care is the date axis. get_code_article reads an article in the version applicable to a given date, and resolve_references grades a citation as found, found with a difference, ambiguous, not found, not applicable at the date, or outside the corpus. Those statuses are not a boolean, and an agent that collapses them into "not found" throws away precisely the signal a reviewer needs. Two self-descriptions earn the entry, both quoted rather than paraphrased: a text absent from the Casus corpus is not a text that does not exist, and the version history is partial, reaching back mostly to 2025, so an earlier date can return "undetermined at the date" because the connector does not guess. Scope is legal:read, the vendor publishes one log line per tool call and states that semantic search queries pass through Voyage AI embeddings and a Pinecone index while the other tools query the corpus database directly. The new slice is a national corpus with versioning and administrative doctrine attached, which neither the US retrieval entry nor the generic EU grounding entry covers. Gap recorded: the tool names come from vendor documentation, not from a driven list, and a trial should settle whether resolve_references returns machine-readable per-citation statuses and whether the call quota stops hard or warns.

    • Sprouts Data MCP - Business Corpus in Any Client · remote Streamable HTTP at https://dashboard.sproutsdata.ai/mcp, a bare initialize answering HTTP 401 with the JSON-RPC error -32000 reading No credential. Send your Sprouts API key as an X-API-Key header (or Authorization: Bearer ...). Keys are issued in the dashboard; sk_dsp_test_ keys hit the same corpus at zero credit cost. That last clause is why this entry carries evidence instead of a card: a test key reads the real corpus, so the surface can be driven before anyone pays. The corpus is 43M+ companies, 200M+ people and 470M affiliation edges, searched across nine categories: companies, people, patents, news articles, trends, market reports, funding rounds, research papers and job openings. Credits are published per tool rather than pooled: a search costs 0.5 Basic or 0.595 AI for the first ten results and 0.08 or 0.085 for each additional one, a record found costs 1 while a miss is free, and sprouts_research_run runs an asynchronous brief from 1.02 to 85 credits by effort, charged only when the run succeeds and resumed by run_id. Two design lines earn the entry. Records carry per-field provenance and the vendor publishes its gaps on purpose, sprouts_coverage returning a not_in_index[] array in plain language, which is the difference between a record set and a claim about the world. Reads cover candidate search by text, semantic or natural language and by stage, a vacancy shortlist ordered by AI score with the per-criterion breakdown and the disqualifying requirements, the full profile with CV link and application answers, interview transcripts with speaker identification and a keyword search across every transcript at once, pipelines with average days per stage and organisation KPIs, and candidate email still unread. The design line is permission parity: each tool requires the permission of its in-app equivalent, a tool the role cannot use is never offered, queries stay inside the caller's company, and confidential searches remain invisible. One discovery quirk is recorded with it, the host-root /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource answering 200 while the /mcp suffix form answers 404.     • Emailit MCP - Send, Deliver and Debug Email From Chat · remote Streamable HTTP at https://api.emailit.com/mcp, answering a bare initialize with HTTP 401 and {"code":-32000,"message":"Authorization Bearer token required"}, with WWW-Authenticate naming https://api.emailit.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp. The vendor's documentation, updated 2 October 2026, states 135 tools covering the full API v2, sign-in by OAuth 2.1 with PKCE or an API key as a bearer token, an access token lasting 15 minutes and a refresh token good for 60 days of inactivity that rotates on every use, where reusing an old one revokes the connection. The line that earns the entry is workspace scoping: consent picks all workspaces or a subset, and any call may name a workspace by ID or exact name without changing the connection default, so two client accounts can be worked in two conversations at once. It sits beside AhaSend, which sends one message and returns a result, and covers what actually breaks: sending domains and their authentication records, audiences, campaigns and the bounce investigation that follows a customer asking why they never got it.

    • LeadSync MCP - Meta Lead Ads Into Your CRM From Chat · local stdio from npm as @leadsync/mcp 0.1.1, installed by npx -y @leadsync/mcp with LEADSYNC_API_KEY in the environment and Node 20 or later, plus a companion skills package that registers the server for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or every one of them at once and stores the key in ~/.leadsync/.env after login. This is the least-privilege shape this catalogue has recorded for files: the member opens one room in an end-to-end encrypted vault to the agent, literally pairing with a six-character code typed into the Terebyte app under Rooms, Connect an agent, and chooses what the agent may do and for how long. The vendor states the boundary as the product, that the agent sees that room and nothing else, and everything is encrypted and decrypted on the computer running the server so the vendor's own servers hold sealed bytes. Inside the room it lists, reads and writes files, makes a Sealed Link, and uses the room's board. Against the catalogue's drive and document entries, which open a whole account until the credential is revoked, this is a consent design rather than an access-control setting, and the trade is stated honestly: a lost key is lost, because the vendor cannot recover what it cannot read.

The design decision recorded here is the local SQLite cache with threading, full-text search and folder synchronisation, because an assistant that re-reads a mailbox from the server on every question is useless above a few thousand messages, and mail_search can read the cache or the server while mail_sync reconciles the two. The failure this one addresses is not forgetting but remembering something that stopped being true: an evidence-backed SQLite store where a correction retires the memories that depended on it instead of sitting beside them as a newer opinion, with exact replay and bisect so a disagreement about what the agent knew can be settled by returning to a state rather than by argument. Recall is hybrid retrieval with cross-encoder reranking, and the local engine needs no model API key, no database server and no Docker, so the accumulated context of a business stays on the machine that already holds the data.

Around that: preview_nfse validates against the official layout or the municipal provider and computes IBS and CBS before anything is transmitted, issue_nfse waits about twenty-five seconds for authorized, rejected, blocked or pending, correction runs by substitution (get_substitution_draft then substitute_document pointing at the original) rather than deletion, lookup_cnpj pulls the Receita record and reports whether the municipality uses the national system, search_service_codes resolves the LC 116 cTribNac and NBS codes, import_invoice reads an XML the company already issued and completes registrations, regime and numbering from it, upload_certificate takes the A1 certificate and create_onboarding_link makes the company owner supply it, create_export builds a per-company and per-month zip plus a spreadsheet carrying the fiscal key on a one-hour signed URL with seven-day retention, and share links are read-only with expiry and revocation. Limitations recorded: Brazil only with Portuguese tool text and rejections, setup needs an A1 certificate and municipal credentials that how_to_get documents rather than fetches, the repository is a manifest with the product code private, and no call was executed because the endpoint refuses everything without a key. Catalogued because the approval step is a default rather than a policy, which is the only version of it that survives an agent having a bad minute.

    🆕 October 27, 2026 - Midday Supplement (2 New, 2 Guides)¶

    An hour after the midday pass, so breadth was skipped and the work went to the three surfaces that move at this gap. mcp.so /feed page one came back with the same newest card, 2026-10-27T16:33:59Z, and the same thirty cards, so nothing arrived there. mcpservers.org /all came back with the same newest slugs the midday pass had dispositioned. The submission window advanced by one, #6243 at 17:53:46Z, and re-reading the feed names against the catalog with the vendor suffix stripped turned up one name that was never ledgered, which the midday pass had not named in its report. Both finds were driven, not just described: one answered a full tools/list and four tools/call executions with no key, the other answered tools/list and three executions with no key.

    🆕 October 27, 2026 - Midday Sweep (6 New, 6 Guides)¶

    Nearly nine hours after the night pass the listing had moved by seven, 17,714 to 17,721, the smallest move measured on this surface all week, and page one had rotated again, so breadth cost three fetches and the weight went to the two surfaces that do move at this gap: the feed, which carried seven cards after the night cutoff, and the submission window, which advanced from #6214 to #6242 with twenty-seven issues and no #6237. Four of the six finds answer initialize with a refusal that states its own terms, two answer with the whole tool surface open and no key at all, and one pair completes a comparison the night pass named and deferred rather than half-documented.

    • FlipProfit MCP - Marketplace Fees to the Cent · remote Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.fliprofit.com/mcp, no auth at all, read-only, GET only upstream with CORS open, by FlipProfit (fliprofit.com). Driven end to end without a key: initialize returned HTTP 200 as fliprofit-mcp 1.2.0, tools/list returned three tools (calculate_fees, compare_platforms, get_fee_changes), and compare_platforms was executed against live rates for a $50 sale with a $10 item cost and $7.50 shipping, returning thirteen platforms ranked by profit: Vinted $32.50 on no fee, Depop $30.40, TikTok Shop $29.50, Reverb $27.91, Mercari and Facebook Marketplace $27.50, Etsy $27.30, Grailed $27.26, Whatnot $26.75, TCGplayer $25.57, eBay $25.30, Amazon $24.01 and Poshmark $22.50, each with its calculator link. The distinction this entry exists to make is that a resale marketplace and a storefront price the same item against different schedules, and the delta between the best and worst platform here is 44 percent of the profit on an identical sale. Beyond the arithmetic, get_fee_changes returns dated fee changes each with the platform's own source URL and the date FlipProfit last verified it, published also as an Atom feed, and every 4xx and 5xx is RFC 9457 application/problem+json with a stable code. Documented upstream surface read alongside: OpenAPI 3.1, /api/v1/fees/<platform>, /api/v1/compare, /api/v1/fees for valid options and an llms.txt. Limitations recorded: US rates in USD only, compare_platforms uses each platform's default options so a category or seller tier has to be passed on calculate_fees before a margin is quoted, fee rules in force on a past date and change reminders sit behind Fee Watch at $6 a month or $60 a year with a 600 request per minute key, and the vendor key list documents twelve platforms while the live tool description carries thirteen with Vinted reachable. Catalogued as the item the night pass named first for this cycle, and because the alternative is a model computing marketplace fees from memory.

    • Seller Profit Doctor MCP - Storefront Profit Math · remote Streamable HTTP at https://sellerprofitdoctor.com/api/mcp with SSE responses, no auth and no sign-in on the free tools, registry com.sellerprofitdoctor/free-tools, by Seller Profit Doctor. initialize returned HTTP 200 as sellerprofitdoctor-free-tools 1.5.0 and tools/list returned sixteen tools, one more than the vendor page documents, across Etsy, Shopify and Amazon: sellerprofit_checkup returning a grade word with level 1 to 5, sellerprofit_etsy_fees and sellerprofit_etsy_profit line by line including payment processing charged on tax and the Offsite Ads cut, sellerprofit_offsite_ads, sellerprofit_shipping_gap, sellerprofit_ads_breakeven, sellerprofit_price_for_margin, sellerprofit_sale_breakeven for how many extra orders a discount needs to hold the same monthly profit, sellerprofit_compare_fees across all three platforms, sellerprofit_ads_roas_breakeven, sellerprofit_box_billing on dimensional weight, sellerprofit_shopify_plan_fit, sellerprofit_shopify_order_fees, sellerprofit_amazon_fees, sellerprofit_amazon_ads_breakeven and sellerprofit_rates for the fee table the numbers use. The containment is the honesty of the output: every result lists the defaults it filled in, Amazon fulfilment, storage and returns carry estimate: true and sit outside the loss total because Amazon measures size and stock, a check-up with too few answers returns no grade and a grade.missing list instead of inventing one, and each fixture's dollar value is scoped to the condition that orders hold. Paired here with FlipProfit because they answer different questions: storefront economics against resale economics, and the second question, whether the ad spend, the discount and the box size leave anything behind. Limitations recorded: US rates, Etsy is the default platform so platform must be set for Shopify or Amazon, the paid full-report surface is a separate endpoint so a free-wired assistant cannot run up a bill, and the Offsite Ads share defaults to 10 percent, the figure Etsy gave at launch in 2020, flagged as a default when the seller does not know it.

    • SpendQuery MCP - Federal Contract Data for Agents · remote Streamable HTTP at https://api.spendquery.com/mcp, no auth and no sign-in, read-only, by SpendQuery (spendquery.com). initialize returned HTTP 200 advertising tools, prompts and resources with instructions that are a method rather than a pitch (call get_catalog once for metrics, dimensions, the QueryPlan schema and worked examples, then write the plan), and tools/list returned thirteen tools against the twelve named in the vendor's llms.txt: get_catalog, run_plan, search_codes, search_recipients, browse_codes, get_notice, size_standard, naics_finder, vehicle_match, search_far, get_far_section, search_local_bids and sbir_awards. run_plan is the reason to catalogue it: the answer returns with status ok, clarify, unsupported or error, a one-paragraph answer, the query and the SQL, so a figure can be re-run and checked instead of accepted, and an out-of-coverage question is declined rather than guessed. Data read from the vendor pages: USAspending.gov prime awards FY2023 through FY2026 dated through Sep 30, 2026, open SAM.gov contract notices, the FAR and DFARS as codified in the eCFR, SBA size standards under 13 CFR 121.201, SBIR and STTR awards since 1983, and state, county and city bids where those governments publish them as open data, most sources refreshing daily with the as-of date shown. The line that matters for an operator is stated in the server's own instructions: amounts are obligations, money committed, not outlays. What travels with each task is the finding: the screenshot or screen recording, the URL, the CSS selector, the client comment, the attachments and the technical details captured when the client clicked, plus console output and replay where the plan includes them. The risk is named rather than smoothed over, because add_comment writes to a surface a paying client reads, so an agent posting "fixed, redeployed" before the deploy is live has told the client something untrue in the thread they watch; the vendor's own framing, that the human reviews what was done on the board or in the thread, is recorded here as the correct default. Containment recorded: the permission set mirrors the connecting user's existing BugHerd permissions, the organization chosen at connect time bounds what the client can reach, and connected clients can be reviewed and revoked, all of which make client separation a property of the connection rather than of a prompt. Clients named by the vendor: Claude Code, Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, VS Code with Copilot, Windsurf, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Zed and Onyx. Limitations recorded: no tool was executed because every path needs an account, what the client attached reaches the assistant recordings included, console and replay depend on the plan and the site integration, and BugHerd reports what a person saw rather than what is broken.

Driven without a key: initialize returned HTTP 200 as "Receipts & invoices to spreadsheet" 0.1.0 and tools/list returned two tools with complete schemas: extract_documents taking files, country, currency, date_order, exports, quickbooks_currency and quickbooks_date_format, and create_upload taking bytes and filename and returning a one-hour signed URL for anything over 2 MB up to 100 MB.     • WatchCron MCP - Know When a Job Stops Reporting · local stdio through npx -y watchcron-mcp, published on npm as watchcron-mcp 1.0.0 with a watchcron-mcp bin and the repository watchcron/watchcron-mcp, authenticated with WATCHCRON_API_KEY, by WatchCron (watchcron.com). No endpoint to probe, and that is recorded rather than worked around: mcp.watchcron.com does not resolve and watchcron.com/mcp refuses a POST with HTTP 405, so the evidence is the package and its README, which documents nine tools: list_monitors with a tag filter, get_monitor, create_monitor from an interval or a cron expression returning the ping URL to add to the job, update_monitor for schedule, grace period and tags, pause_monitor, delete_monitor, get_pings, get_incidents and list_channels. The model is a dead man's switch, which is the only monitoring shape that catches a job that fails silently: the job sends one HTTP request when it finishes and silence past the grace period is the alert, so nothing has to expose a port or install an agent, and curl or wget is enough. Alert routing read from the vendor site: email, Slack, Discord, Google Chat, Matrix, Mattermost, ntfy, Opsgenie, PagerDuty, RocketChat, SMS and webhook, on the same account as uptime, domain and SSL expiry, port, blocklist and cloud cron monitors. Risks recorded as rules rather than warnings: a monitor that never receives a ping reads healthy, a grace period tighter than the job's real runtime pages until the team stops reading the pages, delete_monitor is permanent and takes the history with it, and the API key is an operational credential that can create, pause and delete monitors. Catalogued because the jobs an operator actually needs watched are the ones nobody looks at, and because the ping-URL pattern is the version of this that gets wired up.

    • Veyra MCP - Spend Limits for an Agent That Can Pay · remote Streamable HTTP at https://veyra.money/api/mcp, registry io.github.zapxlabs/veyra 0.1.0, non-custodial USDC on Base. This is the rare remote endpoint that answers more than it refuses: initialize returned HTTP 200 as server veyra 0.1.0 on protocol 2025-06-18, tools/list returned 200 with seven tools (get_capabilities, get_budget, list_payment_sources, create_payment, get_payment, list_payments, cancel_payment), and only tools/call returned 401 MISSING_CREDENTIAL, so the schema is public and the account is not. The containment model is the reason it is catalogued, and the vendor states its own limits plainly: limits must stay consistent (auto-approve at or below ask, ask at or below per-payment, per-payment at or below daily) and a policy that violates that is rejected at edit time with a reason; payments under auto-max proceed with no prompt, the ask band returns awaiting_approval with a one-time link that lapses after 24 hours, and anything over the ask band or the daily cap is blocked server-side. Auto-pay works through a capped ERC-20 approve to a relayer the vendor operates, and the documentation is blunt that the token contract caps how much the relayer may move but not who it may move funds to, which is the policy engine, with the recipient allowlist as the only control on destination. Also recorded: a simulated rail that returns confirmed_simulated with simulated: true and is labelled in the API, the dashboard and the tool description so it can never be reported as a real payment, an audit log of 7 days on Free and 90 on Pro and a year on Team with the events that widen authority named (source.allowance_granted, agent.policy_updated with limits before and after, agent.credential_rotated), and USDC on Base only so policy limits stay exact without a price feed.     🆕 October 26, 2026 - Late Sweep (5 New, 5 Guides)¶

    Eleven hours after the midday pass the listing had moved by three, 17,522 to 17,525, with page one in the identical order, so breadth was repetition and the pass spent its weight where a delta lands at this gap: the submission window, which advanced from #6176 to #6196 with no gaps, the feed, which rotated cards in at the top, and the endpoints themselves. Four of the five finds answer initialize with HTTP 401, which made the discovery documents the primary evidence: a protected-resource document names the resource and the scopes an agent can hold, an authorization-server document states whether a client can register itself and whether PKCE is mandatory, and the difference between a server publishing six separate scopes and one publishing a single coarse scope is visible before anyone signs in.

    • PickFu MCP - Consumer Research Panels an Assistant Can Run · remote Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.pickfu.com/mcp, OAuth behind WorkOS with a device-code grant, registry com.pickfu/mcp 1.0.0, by PickFu (pickfu.com). initialize returned HTTP 401 authentication_required with a resource_metadata pointer in the body, so the contract was read from two documents: the protected-resource response names the resource, one authorization server, header bearer tokens, identity scopes only (openid, email, profile, offline_access) and a WorkOS jwks_uri; the authorization-server response names authorize, device authorization and introspection endpoints on auth.pickfu.com, client_id_metadata_document_supported: true, PKCE S256 and grants for authorization code, refresh token and device code. Vendor-documented surface: save_survey with create, update and template-draft modes, publish_survey, stop_survey with unused responses refunded, delete_survey, get_survey with questions, options, AI summaries and a per-question results object carrying vote totals and the winner, get_survey_responses paginated with explanations, demographics, stored translations and van Westendorp price answers, add_respondents, rate_response and pin_response for panel quality, export_survey_results in CSV, PDF and PNG with short-lived signed CSV links, list_available_targeting and list_available_reporting, build_poll_url, template and tag tools, an upload session for local files (a browser link, a pfuh_ token and an expiry about fifteen minutes out), generate_image with MCP Apps inline cards, and a feature-gated synthetic-audience set that must not be submitted without explicit approval and must not be mixed with human results. The money path is why it is catalogued: publish_survey spends the account's credit balance and then charges the saved card, returning HTTP 402 only when no usable card exists, and the documented flow keeps the poll an unpublished draft, prices it against question types, sample size and targeting, and waits for approval before that call - preview, price, approve, then spend. Limitations recorded: no tool was executed because every path needs an account, the approval gate lives in client behaviour rather than in scope, multi-question surveys are priced per question and an added open-ended "why" question wastes a slot because an explanation is already mandatory on every response, synthetic audiences are beta and feature-gated, mine: true on list_surveys requires OAuth so the two credential paths are not equal, and a preference result is not demand. Catalogued because the consumer-research class was empty in this catalog and because a validated name, package or price is the most expensive thing a small brand gets wrong.
    • AXL MCP - Courses, CRM, Checkout and Email Behind One Agent Surface · remote Streamable HTTP at https://app.axl.tech/mcp, stateless and POST-only, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE, no registry entry found, by AXL EdTech Booster, LLC (axl.tech). A GET answered with the clearest refusal read this cycle: HTTP 405 and this MCP server is stateless - it exposes no GET SSE stream and no DELETE session termination. Send JSON-RPC over POST. initialize without a token returned 401. The protected-resource document publishes scopes_supported: ["mcp"]; the authorization-server document publishes a registration endpoint at /oauth/register (an RFC 7591 public client), token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported: ["none"], PKCE S256, authorization code and refresh grants and a revocation endpoint. Vendor-stated surface: roughly 1,100 account operations behind a small fixed tool set the agent navigates itself - courses and LMS with lessons, hosted video, auto-graded tests and certificates; webinars; community; appointments and paid sessions; landing pages, checkout, order bumps and subscriptions; CRM and pipelines; nine-channel messaging; email campaigns; voice and chat agents; analytics and attribution - and a successful write returns a link to the created record in the admin. The containment is the finding: 21 sensitive operations are removed from the AI surface in the server rather than filtered in a prompt (billing writes, token minting, permission changes, admin creation), the OAuth token is an ordinary admin token under one coarse scope that carries per-field rights, the documented route to a narrower connection is an API key with read rights only, HTML writes refuse until the agent echoes a guide token, and publishing and sending stay separate actions. Limits read from its own documentation: concurrency rather than rate limiting with 429 and Retry-After plus an X-Concurrency-Limit header to read rather than a hard-coded number, uploads that leave the MCP surface for one raw PUT so an MCP-only agent cannot finish one, long responses truncated near 200,000 characters, and a billing-blocked account answering everything except billing reads with 403 lockedSchoolAccessDenied. Limitations recorded: no tool call was executed, the operation count is the vendor's own, and stateless transport means a client requiring an SSE stream needs a bridge such as mcp-remote.
    • Customermates MCP - An Open-Source CRM an Assistant Can Operate · remote Streamable HTTP at https://customermates.com/api/v1/mcp with per-workspace URLs at /api/v1/mcp/w/<WORKSPACE_ID>, OAuth or a 64-character x-api-key, registry io.github.benjiwagner/customermates, core AGPL-3.0 and self-hostable with Docker Compose, by Customermates (customermates.com). initialize returned HTTP 401 {"error":"unauthorized"}; the protected-resource document answers with jwks_uri on its own host, RS256 resource signing and identity scopes. This is the first entry in this catalog's thin CRM class whose core is open source, which removes the vendor from the data path while keeping the same endpoint. The permission model is why it earns a guide: every operation runs inside exactly one workspace, a workspace URL accepts only its own credentials, and the failures are named rather than generic - 406 without the Accept header, 403 workspace_mismatch for another workspace's key, 403 insufficient_permissions when the user's role lacks Read access All on the API and Webhooks row, 403 plan_required for a cloud workspace awaiting its first plan, and a resource_metadata pointer on a wrong-workspace token so the client re-authorizes instead of silently writing. The reference reads as a full CRM rather than a reader: get_workspace_context returning user, company, roles, connected accounts and Knowledge Base in one call, discover_record_types, query_crm_records, search_crm_records, read_crm_record, mutate_crm_record, preview_crm_deletion, import and export, query_crm_measure, messaging and send_email with save and discard drafts, calendars, routines, Knowledge Base pages, roles, teams, webhooks and trash, plus LinkedIn sales lookups. ?toolsets= narrows the surface to records, messaging or workspace. Limitations recorded: no per-key scoping, so a key carries its creator's permissions in full and the narrow instrument is the toolset parameter; the server's confirmation guidance before deleting or sending is explicitly not enforced by the server; messaging, calendar and social tools need a cloud plan at Pro or higher; and no tool call was executed, so names come from the vendor reference rather than a live tools/list.

    • App Store Connect MCP - Sales, Proceeds, Reviews and Releases From Apple's Own API · local stdio Go binary, MIT, brew install idoo/tap/app-store-connect-mcp with the tap answering 200, Docker image and .mcpb bundle, registry io.github.idoo/app-store-connect-mcp at 0.13.0, by Ivan Verevkin (github.com/idoo). No endpoint to probe, so the evidence is the repository's generated tool reference: 76 tools, each tagged read, write or destructive, with a confirm mode of none, flag, plan or human, across sixteen toolsets of which six are on by default. The revenue side is the reason to catalogue it: sales_report returns Sales and Trends aggregates - units by category, proceeds per currency, top-N, with include_rows giving a CSV link - for a period from from/to or frequency plus report_date; analytics_report sums an app's newest analytics segments by dimension on a 24 to 48 hour lag; analytics_setup is the prerequisite that creates the ONGOING report request; insights_summary answers "how is my app doing" in one call with units and proceeds against the previous period plus ratings, versions and TestFlight feedback, each section marked ok or unavailable with the reason; and analytics_funnel_report walks impressions to page views to downloads with conversion by source and territory, sessions, crashes, installs against deletions and a previous-period comparison. Releases are a workflow rather than a bag of REST calls: release_status preflights a version, release_prepare applies a plan_id, release_submit submits the version with IAPs and subscriptions, release_publish releases, release_phased drives a seven-day rollout and release_cancel empties a draft. Anything public or hard to undo is destructive class with a human gate through elicitation, raw API calls validate against a pinned spec before running, and doctor checks key, JWT, Apple reachability, clock skew, rate limit and write mode with a fix per finding. Limitations recorded: local stdio only so nothing was executed here, an App Store Connect API key per team is a real credential with account reach, analytics lags 24 to 48 hours and the funnel needs analytics_setup first, reviewer messages live only in the Resolution Center, and this is a young single-maintainer project at 1 star and version 0.13.0. This is the account-side complement to AppSigma, which reads the public store as a market rather than the account as a ledger.

    • POD Benchmark MCP - Print-on-Demand Supplier Costs · remote Streamable HTTP at https://podbenchmark.com/api/mcp, no auth at all, read-only, 120 requests per minute per IP, official registry entry com.podbenchmark/podbenchmark, by POD Benchmark (podbenchmark.com). Driven end to end without a key: initialize returned HTTP 200 as podbenchmark 1.0.0 on protocol 2025-06-18 advertising tools and resources, tools/list returned ten tools with full JSON schemas, and two calls were executed against live data. list_suppliers returned seven suppliers with their vendor pages: Printful, Printify, Gelato, CustomCat, Prodigi, Inkthreadable and Fourthwall, the last two flagged type: direct rather than marketplace. list_categories returned destination: US, currency: USD and per-category counts with starting delivered prices: Apparel 1,971 products of which 1,722 carry a price across six suppliers from $11.33, T-Shirts 457 products with 389 priced from $12.08, Hoodies 277 products with 232 priced from $12.08. The rest of the surface is the comparison itself: compare_product takes a canonicalProductId with a destination and currency and returns which supplier is cheaper, get_product_options prices one product in a named size or colour, and resolve_supplier_link accepts a pasted supplier URL from any of the seven and returns the normalized product, which is the step that makes a like-for-like comparison possible without a shared product id. Limitations recorded: the normalization is the vendor's and a wrong merge produces a confident wrong comparison, one apparel product in eight has no price, other destinations and currencies are parameters rather than defaults, and tax, shipping terms and returns sit outside the server, so this compares cost and not landed obligation. Catalogued as a reversal of the August 26 hold on BestPrintOnDemand, which was held as a thin site-published comparison: the evidence that changes the disposition is ten live tools, keyless execution returning real supplier and category payloads, per-size and per-colour pricing and a supplier-link resolver across seven suppliers, which is a procurement surface rather than a price table.

The finding is in the discovery documents: the WWW-Authenticate header points at https://mcp.gbply.net/functions/v1/mcp/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, which answers {"error":"not_found","use":"https://mcp.gbply.net/v1"}, while the live document at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource returns resource: https://mcp.gbply.net/v1, an authorization server at https://mcp.gbply.net/oauth, header bearer tokens and no scopes_supported field at all, and that server's metadata returns scopes_supported: ["email","profile","offline_access"] with PKCE S256 and response_types_supported: ["code"]. Identity scopes only, no reviews:write and no posts:write: authorization over business data lives in the product's request system rather than in the token, the opposite of the eight resource scopes Leadpages MCP publishes. Capability from the vendor connector documentation: read on workspaces, profiles, completeness, insights running 2-3 days behind, monthly search terms, reviews and rating stats, posts, photos, Q&A, Profile Guard changes, Rank Tracker and citation scans, analysis reports and credit balances; draft with nothing saved for AI review replies, Q&A suggestions and rank-scan cost previews; a request for every publish, schedule, edit or delete of a reply or post, every saved FAQ, every profile field, every Profile Guard decision and every paid scan; and direct only for a Google sync a few times an hour. Requests expire in fifteen minutes and run once, and on approval the vendor re-checks permission, credits, plan limits and the daily post cap, keeping a post that fails policy as flagged rather than published. An optional per-action Always allow covers publish, profile change, spend credits with a most-per-request and a most-per-24-hours limit, and deletes of things not yet live, scoped to one assistant in one workspace, overridable by the workspace owner and only switchable from a 2FA sign-in in a 2FA workspace, with every auto-approved action labelled as such. Permissions are inherited, so a viewer can read and draft but cannot create requests, staff and admin features are never reachable through the connector, and demo profiles are read-only. Limitations recorded: the tool schemas were not read, Google performance data lags two to three days, billing and workspace membership are deliberately outside the connector, and OpenGMB is the self-hosted open-core alternative for teams who will not send profile data to a vendor. Catalogued because the write side of the profile is where local businesses lose, and because the approval contract here is the cleanest example in this catalog of an agent that can prepare everything and commit almost nothing, beside localith-mcp for read-only profile analysis and listings-api-mcp for citations.

    🆕 October 25, 2026 - Late Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)¶

    The directory did not move in five and a half hours: 17,360 servers at the midday capture and 17,360 at the 23:26Z read, with page one carrying the same thirty cards in the same order. A frozen listing makes the breadth work repetition, so this pass spent its reads on the two surfaces that did move, the feed, which rotated five new cards in after the supplement cutoff, and the submission window, which filed twenty-one issues between #6111 and #6131. Three of the finds are business systems, and each one needed a different kind of proof: one answered without a key, and two published their capability in their own OAuth discovery documents because their tool lists sit behind a sign-in.

Two calls executed: domain_trust on example.com returned verdict: likely_safe, risk_score: 0, age_days: 11396, blocklist_listings: 0, https_valid: true, not_checked: [] and method: Rule-based: domain age, blocklists, TLS. A heuristic, not a guarantee. with a receipt of rail: sample, charge_usd: 0.0; domain_email_auth returned ok: true with spf: {status: pass, record: "v=spf1 -all"}, via dns.pizza, and a cache block that reported a stale hit at ageSeconds: 23212 instead of passing it off as live. A non-sample call returns HTTP 402 carrying the whole x402 v2 offer rather than a signup wall, network: eip155:8453 on Base mainnet, USDC 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, amount_atomic: 20000, payTo: 0xa76a0E93C5af3fd43521300B0a58eF5F70fC44F6 and a 300 second window, with a credit rail and an add_credit link that funds a key from $5 without revealing it. Limitations recorded: the trust verdict is a three-signal heuristic and says so in its own response, page_watch needs a first call to store a baseline before it can report a change, and the email check reads published records rather than testing a mailbox.     • More AI Fortnox MCP - Swedish Books, Approved Writes · remote Streamable HTTP at https://accounting.amore.cloud/mcp, OAuth sign-in through Fortnox with exactly two scopes, fortnox:read and fortnox:write published at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource after both initialize and tools/list returned HTTP 401 invalid_token, registry cloud.amore.accounting/fortnox at 1.0.2 with an accounting-firm edition registered as cloud.amore.byra/fortnox, by Starberg & More Solutions AB. Live probe: unauthenticated POST initialize returned HTTP 200 with serverInfo lintelly-hr-deutschland 0.2.0 on protocol 2025-06-18, capabilities for tools, prompts and resources, and an instruction block that restricts the server to German employment and social insurance law and tells an assistant to answer questions about Austria, Switzerland or anywhere else with the sentence that this server only knows German law. tools/list returned 38 tools across workflows, deadlines, money, leave, obligations, document drafts, 126 contract clause blocks and a dated legal-value lookup. Six real tools/call executions: arbeitgeberkosten on a 1,800 euro part-time role returned uebergangsbereich: true, summe_arbeitgeber: null and mindestens_arbeitgeber: 380.70, with health and long-term care at 10.55 percent (189.90 euro) and pension plus unemployment at 10.6 percent (190.80 euro), the paragraph governing the Midijob transition band, and a plain statement that the payroll office computes the exact figure rather than guessing it; kuendigungsfrist_rechnen on entry 2024-03-01, receipt 2026-10-30, employer side and six months probation returned an end on 2026-11-30, a latest receipt date of 2026-10-31, the rule as one month to month end under section 622(2) of the Civil Code, two full years of service, probation ended 2024-08-31 and the next three end dates, with the trap that a weekend or holiday end date does not move because section 193 does not apply to notice periods; minijob at 13.90 euro an hour and 8 hours a week returned the 603.00 euro monthly and 7,236.00 euro annual limits, a maximum of 43.38 hours a month (10.01 a week), 34.64 planned hours at 481.50 euro, and employer levies itemised at health 13 percent 62.60, pension 15 percent 72.22, flat-rate tax 2 percent 9.63, U1 0.8 percent 3.85, U2 0.22 percent 1.06 and insolvency 0.15 percent 0.72, 150.08 in total for 631.58 euro of monthly cost, plus the 2027 change to 14.60 euro and 633.00 euro; urlaubsanspruch on 30 contract days at three days a week returned 18 working days split into 12 statutory (24 working days times 3 divided by 6) and 6 contractual, with the warning that leave forfeits only after a specific written warning; schwellen_check at six employees returned that a works council may be elected from five, that the U1 levy runs to thirty and that a four-week contractual notice period is allowed to twenty, and that dismissal protection needs more than ten, the part-time claim more than fifteen and a break room more than ten, each missing by five; and rechtswert on minimum wage at 2026-11-01 returned 13.90 euro for 2026, 14.60 euro from 2027-01-01, the full dated series back to 2024, the Fifth Minimum Wage Adjustment Ordinance as the norm, an official gesetze-im-internet.de link and a next review date of 2026-11-15. Every answer carries the same shape, ergebnis, rechenweg, quellen with norm, official link, check date and confirmation status, fallen, naechster_schritt, hinweis, stand and herausgeber, and several source rows say plainly that the rate is not yet confirmed, which is the opposite of a confident stale number. Open and free: code MIT, legal content CC BY 4.0, name and logo reserved, no credit, plan or tool limit, with the vendor's paid HR service for companies from ten employees behind it and at most one sentence and link pointing there when a case warrants a person. Official registry entry com.lintelly/hr-deutschland 0.2.0 active since 2026-10-23T15:58:52Z, published as npm @lintelly/hr-deutschland 0.2.0 and ghcr.io/nicksadvisory/lintelly-hr-deutschland:0.2.0 for stdio and as the streamable HTTP remote. Limitations recorded rather than smoothed over: Germany only with no Austrian or Swiss or EU layer, general information and not legal advice for a case, the employer share in the 603.00 to 2,000.00 euro transition band given as a lower bound rather than a total, the U1 and U2 levies and the employers liability contribution outside every cost figure so a budget built only here comes out low, document tools that produce text and transmit nothing, no connection to a payroll or HR system, per-tool daily call counts in coarse bands even though inputs are not stored, and a repository created 2026-10-23 and pushed 2026-10-24 with 0 stars, 0 forks and one open issue under a single publishing account.

Pricing from the vendor's own page: trial EUR 0 for 7 days with 50 credits and no card, Premium EUR 98 per month plus VAT with 1 market and 200 credits a month, EUR 10 per extra user and EUR 15 per extra department workspace, credit packs at EUR 9 for 100, EUR 39 for 500 and EUR 99 for 1,500, and Enterprise for unlimited markets with full API access, scheduled exports, SSO and an SLA. Catalog gap closed: the procurement class here held EU TED notices and Texas ESBD solicitations, both single-source readers delivered over Apify with the operator's own token, and neither joined a notice to its award history - take-rate for a supplier is who already wins that buyer's work, and nothing in the catalog could answer it. Limitations recorded rather than smoothed over: the market count is stated four ways on the vendor's own surfaces (50+ on the MCP root page, 78 on the data API page, 80+ on the Claude and ChatGPT pages, 89 in the dated coverage snapshot), the MCP surface is narrower than the platform since monitoring, exports and document analysis live on the platform and the Enterprise API, one market per plan unit makes a multi-country question a multiple of the headline price, and award values, amendments, lots and award notices can describe the same procedure more than once. Gap named rather than claimed: no tool call was made, because every tool needs an OAuth connection to an account this sweep does not create, so the entry rests on the live 401, the protected-resource and authorization-server metadata, the endpoint's own tool documentation and the vendor's pricing and methodology pages. Break-even price $10.24 per unit" with the final value fee line stating "13.6% on the portion up to $7,500; 2.35% on the portion over $7,500 (per item, on the total amount of the sale incl. shipping and tax)", the per-order fee $0.40 on "order total $30.00 > $10" and promoted listings $1.50 at "5% of $30.00"; etsy_fees at price 24.99, shipping_charged 5, offsite_ads_pct 15, region us returned "$7.80 (26% of revenue)" from listing $0.20, transaction $1.95 at 6.5%, processing $1.15 at "3% of $29.99 + 0.25 USD" and Offsite Ads $4.50 at "15% of $29.99, max 100 per order"; amazon_fees at price 29.99, category home-kitchen, fulfillment fba, 10 x 8 x 4 inches, 1.5 lb, ship_date 2026-11-20 returned "$11.66 (38.89% of revenue)" with referral $4.50 at 15% and a $0.30 minimum, FBA fulfilment $6.49 priced on "Large standard, 2.3 lb shipping weight, peak standard card" (dimensional weight beating the 1.5 lb entered, since 10 x 8 x 4 inches is 320 cubic inches) and a $0.23 fuel and logistics surcharge that appears only inside the October 15 to January 14 peak window; compare_marketplaces at price 34.99, item_cost 9, shipping_label_cost 4.5, shipping_charged 5, target_margin_pct 30 returned Etsy $22.24 profit at 55.62%, eBay $20.65 at 51.64% and Amazon FBA $13.58 at 38.8%, with Amazon revenue at $34.99 rather than $39.99 because FBA shipping is set by Amazon and the buyer's $5 never arrives; amazon_target_price at category home-kitchen, fulfillment fba, target_margin_pct 30, item_cost 9 returned "list at $29.39 for a 30% margin; break-even $19.02", solved rather than divided because the referral percentage and the fulfilment band both move with the price. Tools: 69 published, 49 of them the agent's own and 20 for accounts, integrations, campaign drafts, automations, Knowledge and job status, each documenting its inputs, its per-operation permission, the role it needs and its error contract, with tools/list returning only what the connection's permissions and the caller's role allow. Three access shapes are declared per tool: read, change (acts at once and needs an idempotency key) and proposal for approval. A proposal returns status: awaiting_approval, an actionId, a field-by-field preview, an expiresAt and a link at adrails.ai/oauth/actions/<actionId>; any current owner or admin of the workspace approves it signed in as themselves, Adrails re-reads the platform and applies the exact change once or blocks it if the entity moved, and the proposal expires 24 hours after it was prepared (30 minutes in-app). Budget changes cap at 30% each, an increase needs measured spend and results, bulk selection covers at most 40 entities, and everything Adrails creates starts paused. Idempotency is enforced rather than advisory, errors return as tool results with isError so the model can correct the call, a result over 256,000 bytes is refused whole with no partial figures, and limits run 60 calls a minute per token, 10 changes a minute, 180 a minute per person and 600 per workspace. Business sources read beside ad spend: Shopify, Stripe, Klaviyo, Triple Whale, PostHog, RevenueCat and Google Drive. Two tools carry the entry. store_revenue returns gross, refunded and net sales kept apart, in each store's own currency, never converted. business_review accepts an explanation only when every number quotes its source word for word, from the person's own statement or from a tool result in the connection's history, which is a provenance rule enforced inside the tool rather than a disclaimer beside it. budget_recommend compares the latest two complete seven-day windows in the account's time zone and suggests no amount. Plans from the vendor's own page: Preview free with 10 credits once, Starter $49 a month with 200 credits, Growth $149 with 700, Scale $399 with 2,000, unlimited ad accounts and team members on every paid plan, every connector included, no percentage of ad spend, and MCP tool calls at zero credits. Gap named rather than claimed: no tool call was made, because every tool needs an OAuth connection to a workspace with a connected ad account, so the entry rests on the live 401, the protected-resource metadata, the server card and the vendor's 69-tool reference.

    • Muvia BI MCP - Governed Data Platform for Agents · remote server at https://api.muviabi.com/mcp/v1, JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP POST with the answer arriving as one SSE data line, protocol 2025-06-18, by Superduck S.r.l. (muviabi.com). Live probe: unauthenticated POST initialize returned HTTP 401 with www-authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://api.muviabi.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/v1/"; that document returned HTTP 200 with resource https://api.muviabi.com/mcp/v1/, an authorization server on the same host and bearer_methods_supported: ["header"], and the authorization-server metadata returned authorization, token, registration and revocation endpoints, authorization_code and refresh_token grants, code_challenge_methods_supported: ["S256"] and client_id_metadata_document_supported: true. Tools: 231 from the vendor reference, 113 read and 118 write, the writes split 96 proposal, 12 confirmed in Muvia and 10 not available to API keys, across fourteen modules (Flows 36, Lab 26, Assets 24, Alarms 20, Notebooks 19, Dashboards 18, Sources 18, Analysis 17, Nodes 15, Core 12, Project 8, Annotations 7, Predictors 7, Documents 4). The operator surface is the read half: query_sql and describe_sql over the data lake, read_lineage, run_query_checks and set_query_checks, list_quarantine, list_dataset_readers, list_datasets and read_dataset; list_alarms with describe_alarm, investigate_alarm and shelve_alarm; list_dashboards with create_dashboard, add_widget and convert_chart; list_predictors with promote_predictor_version and reject_predictor_version; and get_action for the outcome of a filed write. What earns the entry is that the governance travels inside the protocol: a write never mutates the platform on the spot, it files a proposal that a person approves in Muvia or the company policy applies, a key writes only when an administrator has turned on writes through assistants for it, an administrator can grant a key only scopes they hold themselves and never superadmin, and the company's enabled modules cap every key. Rate limits are 120 a minute per key and 100,000 a day per company in fixed windows, with X-RateLimit-Limit, -Remaining and -Reset on every response. Gaps named rather than claimed: an account is required with the AI connectors module and the only public entry is the 14-day trial at app-demo.muviabi.com/try; /en/pricing and /it/pricing both returned 404, so there is no price list to quote; the protected-resource metadata advertises an empty scopes_supported while the tools declare scopes individually, so scope discovery has to come from tools/list; and no tool call was made, which is the difference between this entry and the three catalogued at midday.
