    🆕 October 21, 2026 - Evening Sweep (2 New, 2 Guides)¶

    An evening delta eight hours after the midday supplement. The feed page repeated itself in full, all thirty cards matching prior dispositions, while mcpservers.org /all newest-first carried the two genuinely new business-relevant slugs. Both catalogued entries were settled by running the endpoint, and one of them by running a real tool call rather than a handshake.

    • UniPost MCP - LinkedIn and X Publishing With Approval · remote Streamable HTTP server at https://mcp.unipost.ai/mcp, OAuth in the browser or a workspace API key, by UniPost (unipost.ai). Live probe: unauthenticated POST initialize returned HTTP 401 carrying the server's own message, {"error":{"code":-32001,"message":"Sign in to UniPost, or create an API key in UniPost → API keys."}}. Seven tools are named in the vendor's reference: list_accounts, list_posts, schedule_post, approve_post, cancel_post, get_analytics and get_x_allowance. Scheduling and approving are separate tools on purpose, schedule_post always creates pending_approval and returns an approval link, a post created by another person's agent cannot be approved through the tool at all, and TikTok posts must be approved on the vendor screen because their privacy settings live there. Pricing is graduated per connected account, two free, $3 for accounts 3 to 10, $1 for 11 to 30 and $0.50 above, yearly at ten times monthly. The X credit model is the operationally load-bearing fact: a plain post costs 1 credit, a post containing a link costs 13, the free allowance is 10 credits a month, and a paid workspace gets 50 per X account for its first ten and 20 after, with 10 posts an hour and 25 a day enforced at publish time rather than at schedule time. Packaged addition, not a gap: the publishing class is six deep here through PendPost, TimeToPost, BulkPublish, Blog2Social, Chirpie and Maeve Social, and this is recorded for the pricing shape and the two-tool approval split.

    • Agents Handbook MCP - Tested Playbooks Before the Run · keyless remote Streamable HTTP server at https://agentshandbook.com/mcp, no sign-in and no key, by Agents Handbook (agentshandbook.com). Probed live and driven: POST initialize returned HTTP 200 (serverInfo agentshandbook 0.1.0, protocol 2025-06-18, tools, resources and prompts capabilities, plus server instructions), tools/list returned eleven tools counted rather than claimed, and a real tools/call on search_playbooks for "reconcile receipts against bank transactions" at min_trust: corroborated returned one playbook, match-receipts-to-bank-transactions-for-your-accountant, graded corroborated and high risk with the four agents it is written for plus page and markdown URLs. Every playbook carries a trust level from reported through corroborated, tested and confirmed, a risk level, and human checkpoints defined as the steps that spend money, send messages, submit forms or delete data. Failures sit in a separate get_lessons surface, report_run writes a worked, worked-with-changes or failed result into a review queue rather than straight into the record, and submit_playbook, submit_use_case, check_submission and register_contributor carry the contribution side. 54 playbooks across ten categories, a markdown twin on every URL, and a plain search endpoint at /api/v1/search?q=. Reverses a title-level hold: the midday supplement held this as an agent-playbook knowledge surface read at title level, and read to detail it earns an entry on mechanism rather than topic, because numbered checkpoints plus an evidence grade per playbook is the closest live analogue to the governance contract this docs set publishes.

    Also identified this cycle (not catalogued): Lead Gen Marketing Intelligence at https://lead-gen-system.upapi.io/api/mcp held on documentation rather than product, because the endpoint is live and gated (HTTP 401 missing authorization header) and the directory promises ten read-only tools across nine social platforms, while /llms.txt and the root both serve the sign-in screen and the listing URL /settings/mcp is a dashboard page returning 307 to login, so an entry would be vendor marketing text with a status code behind it; Polign Recall read this cycle after the midday pass recorded it as a 404 shell, Apache 2.0 with corrections-as-records, as_of, history and diff, held against a dense memory class and noted for sharing the shape of a trust contract; match.bot held as novelty agent infrastructure with no operator data in it; UAIN Research Pilot held as a research marketplace at pilot stage; Waldo held as desktop automation infrastructure on the ShadowCursor and Zeptap precedent; Arquimedes held as a study corpus; and POEditor held as developer tooling. Twenty-six further /all cards carried prior dispositions without re-litigation, and all thirty mcp.so /feed page 1 cards matched an existing sweep record, which is recorded as a source behaviour: at gaps under about twelve hours, /all carries the fresh slugs and the feed repeats.

    🆕 October 21, 2026 - Midday Supplement (2 New, 2 Guides)¶

    A supplement about an hour after the midday capture, run against all three surfaces once more. The directories were unchanged inside the hour, so the delta came from the feed recapture and from the ledger itself: one card was posted past the midday cut at 17:16Z, and three cards the midday report recorded as carried prior dispositions had no ledger entry behind them. All four were read to detail level and every catalogued one was settled by running the endpoint.

    • Shopify Speed Check MCP - Store Speed and Plan Fees · free remote Streamable HTTP server at https://tools.skaidigital.com/mcp, no key and no account, by Skai Digital (skaidigital.com), a headless Shopify agency. Live probe: unauthenticated POST initialize returned HTTP 200 (serverInfo skai-shopify-tools 1.0.0, protocol 2025-06-18) and tools/list returned three tools, counted rather than claimed. check_shopify_store_speed runs PageSpeed Insights on mobile and desktop with real-user Core Web Vitals, returns the bottlenecks ranked, and labels a headless estimate with its assumptions, in 10 to 90 seconds with results cached 24 hours. detect_shopify_store reads the public page only and reports theme store or headless plus the theme name: a live call on allbirds.com returned shopify_theme with theme allbirds-theme and four signals. calculate_shopify_fees prices Basic, Grow, Advanced and Plus for a sales volume and payment mix, with break-even sales between consecutive plans and the requirements only Plus covers; a live call at $250,000 monthly GMV and an $85 average order returned Advanced at $7,766 a month as the cheapest plan that meets the requirements, Basic excluded on staff account limits rather than on price, with break-evens at $30,000, $135,000 and $808,750 in monthly online sales, US prices checked 2026-10-21 and the variable Plus platform fee excluded unless quoted. Catalog gap named rather than closed: the speed class is already here through GTmetrix and Sorank, no entry anywhere is Shopify-specific, and nothing here attributed a slow storefront to the apps a merchant pays for or priced the plan decision underneath it.

    • IQFluence MCP - Creator Vetting and Media Plans · remote Streamable HTTP server at https://mcp.iqfluence.io/mcp, OAuth 2.1 in the browser or an API key for scripts and CI, by IQFluence (iqfluence.io). Live probe: unauthenticated POST initialize returned HTTP 401 {"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"Authentication required"}; /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server returned HTTP 200 publishing authorize, token, register and revoke endpoints, authorization_code and refresh_token grants and PKCE S256, while the protected-resource path returns 404. Fifteen tools are named in the vendor's docs with a credit cost on every paid step: search_influencers over 455M Instagram, TikTok and YouTube profiles with audience filters, the first three rows free and the rest hidden; unlock_search_results at 0.02 credits an account; get_influencer_report at 1 credit and free inside 30 days, carrying audience quality, fake-follower signals, engagement, growth and contacts; compare_influencers and audience_overlap at 1 credit per creator or calculation; build_media_plan at 1 credit per creator for expected views, engagements, CPM and cost per engagement; get_contacts at 0.04 an account; creator, hashtag, post and comment reads at 0.02 a page; and the account surface get_account_balance, list_campaigns, get_campaign_stats and list_my_reports. The assistant states the cost of a paid step and asks before any task above 5 credits, a daily credit limit can be set per assistant key, and every paid request is written to the request history with its parameters, cost and time. Plans are Starter $199 for 300 credits and Pro $299 for 500, yearly at 20 percent off, top-ups $0.79 a credit from 50 and valid three months, and the trial is 5 credits once per account.     Midday delta about seven hours after the night capture, and this one belonged to mcpservers.org /all rather than the feed: pages 1 to 4 through the r.jina.ai reader proxy carried three of the four entries, the chatmcp/mcpso issue window carried the fourth, and the mcp.so /feed page 1 came back with the night cycle's cards plus not much else. All four were settled by running the endpoint, not by reading a listing.

    • Next Everything MCP - BOM Pricing and Ordering for Builds · remote server at https://mcp.nexteverything.io/mcp, bearer API key from the account dashboard, by Next Everything (nexteverything.io). Live probe: unauthenticated POST initialize returned HTTP 401. Eight tools: create_project, check_bom, update_bom_line, find_parts, get_part, find_alternatives, place_order, order_status. The surface is a bill of materials priced for a real build: 630,000+ in-stock parts from the JLCPCB/LCSC library refreshed daily, with DigiKey and Mouser checked live on every line so prices and stock sit side by side, plus manufacturer lifecycle warnings for parts that are not recommended for new designs or are end of life. check_bom returns per-distributor price comparison, the shipments with estimated shipping and a quote_id, and flags rather than repairs: out of stock, not enough stock, uncertain matches, an MPN and a distributor number on one line pointing at different parts, a missing footprint, and the JLCPCB extended-part fee when assembly is requested. update_bom_line re-prices the whole build after a swap, so accepting an alternative is one call and one new quote. place_order requests an order and charges nothing; the team re-checks live stock and price and emails a payment link. Quotes are USD and valid 24 hours, import duties excluded. Catalog gap closed: the only bill-of-materials entry here belongs to a wire-harness diagram tool (Harness Atlas), and nothing priced a build against live distributor stock.

    • AIS Trail MCP - Live Vessel Positions and Port Calls · remote stateless Streamable HTTP server at https://api.aistrail.com/mcp, no key needed for the live tools, by AIS Trail (aistrail.com). Live probe: unauthenticated POST initialize returned HTTP 200 (serverInfo aistrail-ais 1.5.1, protocol 2025-06-18) and tools/list returned 11 tools, counted rather than claimed. Six answer without a key from the same picture as the public live map: search_vessels, get_vessel, vessels_in_area, vessels_near, find_port and data_status. Five need a key and read the archive: vessel_track (raw to 24 hours, one minute to 7 days, one hour to 366 days, 200 points per call), vessel_port_calls, port_calls, vessel_events and lookup_vessels. Port call and event rows carry sanctions, the codes of the lists that name the ship's IMO number, and lookup_vessels returns each listing with its programme and date. Positions are never interpolated, suspicious jumps are flagged rather than deleted, each response carries the source attribution its licence requires (Digitraffic under CC BY 4.0 among them), and private vessels are never listed individually on any plan. Rate limits are 10 calls a second per IP keyless and 20 a second per account with a key; track requests cost 1 credit per vessel day. Plans: Free at 500 credits a month with no card, Starter $29 for 15,000 credits and 12 months of history on a 24 hour delay, Pro $129 with live positions and a WebSocket stream, Business $249 with boxes up to 10 degrees. Catalog gap named rather than closed: the maritime class here was container milestones (Container Tracking over 200+ lines), a Ukrainian vessel registry (Sudnokontrol) and chokepoint intel; none answered what a specific ship is broadcasting right now.

Live probe: unauthenticated POST initialize returned HTTP 401. 29 tools across campaign reads and money reads plus eight writes (set_post_cpm, finalize_post, refresh_post, add_creator, set_creator_offer, set_creator_link, pause_creator, resume_creator). get_payouts_summary is the tool the class needed: owed and final, ready to pay, owed but blocked, payout details to check, held for a views spike, and still counting, each split out rather than totalled into one number. list_payable_creators names who can be paid now and why the rest cannot, list_payment_requests and get_payment_request open a request down to the per-post views that justify it, and list_payment_history records who marked what paid. get_needs_you returns the dashboard's own waiting-on-you list and list_activity returns the log as sentences.     • UXArmy MCP - Run User Research From the Assistant · remote server at https://app.uxarmy.com/mcp, account sign-in on first connect, by UXArmy (uxarmy.com). Live probe: unauthenticated POST initialize returned HTTP 401; uxarmy.com/mcp returns 404 and mcp.uxarmy.com does not resolve, so the app host is the endpoint. The read side searches projects and studies by description with no IDs, extracts themes, sentiment and exact quotes, flags studies below target and tasks nobody reached, pulls transcripts with speaker labels and timestamps in the original language, and opens one participant down to device, every task answer, unreached tasks and a replay link. The act side is what makes it different: recommend the method for a question (usability test, survey, card sort, tree test or interview), build the survey or the study scenario, screener, tasks, rating scales and open questions, trim to a target duration, set panel targeting by country, age and device, draft screener questions, and launch only after the operator says so. Account work covers workspaces, roles, team and projects. Panel recruiting draws on credits bought separately; every plan including Free can invite its own participants. Catalog gap named rather than closed: Uxia covers simulated usability testing and a second entry reads results from tests already run; this is the first here that recruits real participants and launches a live study.

    • Tenantback MCP - CAM Reconciliation Audit · remote server at https://tenantback.com/mcp, no key needed for audits, A2A endpoint alongside it, by Tenantback (tenantback.com). Live probe: unauthenticated POST initialize returned HTTP 200 (serverInfo tenantback 1.0.0 on protocol 2025-06-18) and tools/list returned audit_cam_reconciliation and get_audit_result. A workspace key adds nine more: portfolio_overview, list_locations, get_lease_abstract, search_lease_documents, list_findings, list_deadlines, get_statement, request_audit, get_audit_request, draft_dispute (drafts only, a person approves sending). The audit checks pro-rata share and its denominator, CAM caps cumulative and non-cumulative, admin and management fee rate and base, excluded costs, gross-up above the occupancy threshold, year-over-year variance, the balance due and late statement delivery. The lease quote is verified against the source page and the arithmetic is computed in code, so a finding either balances against the statement line or it does not. Free audits are capped at 5 per sender a day with 10 files per request and 20 MB per file; recovery work is 25% of money actually recovered, and the portfolio plan is $49 per location a month plus 12% of recoveries. Catalog gap closed: every commercial-property entry here concerns managing an asset (Hercules Property, Dutch Property Context, AskRent, LucidRents); none audited the expense reconciliation a tenant is billed for.

    🆕 October 20, 2026 - Evening Sweep (7 Servers, 1 Guide)¶

    Evening delta about seven hours after the midday capture. The mcp.so /feed page 1 returned 30 cards and mcpservers.org /all pages 1 to 3 about 90, and one vendor produced the whole cycle: Copliancy Inc published seven product servers inside a single hour, all for the same customer, and together they close a gap this catalog has carried since it began tracking operations software.

    • Copliancy MCP Suite - Licenses, Leases and Incidents per Location · seven remote servers from Copliancy Inc (copliancy.com), a US multi-location compliance and record platform used across hospitality, grocery, healthcare, oil and gas, transport, education and construction. IncidentVault at https://app.incidentvault.com/api/mcp/apps/server covers incidents, claims, reserves, settlements, legal spend, risk checks, regulatory inspections and tasks in 38 scopes (19 read, 19 write, plus offline_access); its protected-resource document sets bearer_methods_supported: ["header"] and its authorization server publishes authorize, token, registration and revocation endpoints for PKCE S256 with dynamic client registration. PolicyTrak at https://app.policytrak.com/api/mcp covers sites, compliance fields, policies, SOPs, laws, acknowledgements, workflows, files, audit trails and imports across 57 scopes. RetailHardHat at https://app.retailhardhat.com/api/mcp runs site development from due diligence through permits, bids, RFIs, project budgets, change requests and invoices to opening day in 20 scopes. CredentialCamp at https://app.credentialcamp.com/api/mcp tracks credentials, certifications and mandated training in 5. QuipAssist at https://app.quipassist.com/api/mcp is the maintenance layer - equipment, work orders, preventive schedules, parts, vendors, IoT readings - in 13 scopes, one of them documents:sensitive. LeaseCommand at https://app.leasecommand.com/api/mcp carries leases, rent schedules, critical dates and ASC 842 amortization with journal entries. SmartShifts at https://app.smartshifts.com/api/mcp/apps/server covers shifts, coverage, time off and tasks. Verified live this sweep: all seven endpoints answered a POST initialize probe with 401 or 403 and never a 200 without credentials; five publish OAuth protected-resource metadata, SmartShifts returns 404 on that path and LeaseCommand serves its application HTML there, so both are described as declaring scopes without publishing metadata. The design worth reading: every call checks the user's role, location and record limits, so an agent handed to a store manager cannot enumerate another store. IncidentVault documents two surfaces and the difference between them - the operational endpoint returns opaque record IDs, allowlisted status and priority, dates, location IDs and audit percentages while excluding names, narratives, medical details, custom fields and attachments, and the private endpoint keeps the full authorized catalog. Writes are opt-in and every modifying tool produces a saved preview a person approves inside the product; the vendor is explicit that pending or approved is not executed success. MCP Apps hosts render a working dashboard; other hosts get structured facts and source links, and Gemini widget support is not assumed. Free sign-up, tier pricing not published in text. Catalog gap closed: A4B, ZenSched and STEADYWRK cover assets, workforce scheduling and field dispatch as single-purpose tools, and nothing here carried license and permit renewals, incident and claims records, ASC 842 lease accounting or credential compliance across locations.

    • Azquo MCP - Audited Shared Memory for AI Agents · remote server at https://data.azquo.ai/mcp, official (azquo.com), OAuth 2.1 bearer with scope mcp or an API key from the Azquo admin site. Live probe: initialize returned HTTP 401 Unauthorized : no key with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://data.azquo.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource", and that metadata document returns resource https://data.azquo.ai/mcp, authorization server https://data.azquo.ai, bearer_methods_supported: ["header"], scopes_supported: ["mcp"], resource_name: "Azquo". The capability list is the vendor's own wording because no tools/list is reachable without a credential: create databases, import raw files, design and refine import templates, query in AQL, browse and extend hierarchies, build and run reports, and audit any single figure back through every transformation to its source file, user and date, plus rehearse a risky change on a copy, see the history of a name, restore a deleted one and read every earlier value with who changed it and where it came from. The architecture is the reason it earns the entry: names in hierarchies rather than rows in tables, so a new dimension is a new lens over existing data instead of a migration, and provenance is per cell rather than per row.     🆕 October 19, 2026 - Evening Sweep (1 New, 1 Guide)¶

    Evening delta about eight and a half hours after the midday capture, and both directories rotated hard in the window: the mcp.so /feed page 1 (29 server and client links, six of them posted after the 19:30 UTC midday pull) plus mcpservers.org /all pages 1-4 through the r.jina.ai reader proxy (120 cards, 99 of them not named anywhere in the midday sweep or the night sweep before it). The six fresh feed cards were all consumer or developer utilities and were held. One new business-relevant entry, catalogued with a guide: a pre-action mandate gate for agent payments, verified rule by rule against its live endpoint.

    • drift MCP - Pre-Action Mandate Enforcement for AI Agents · remote Streamable HTTP at https://drift.rta.lat/mcp (JSON-RPC 2.0, protocol 2025-06-18, server drift 0.1.0, no auth), Apache-2.0, github.com/mrpkk/drift at default branch master, created October 4, 2026, Python 3.11+, zero dependencies: the missing check between an agent being granted a payment mandate and the money leaving. AP2 verifies the mandate once at signature time and then steps away; drift re-checks six rules in a fixed order before every action - amount, payee, audience, currency, window, intent - with DENY as the default and the refusal naming the most important rule rather than an incidental one. Three tools, all annotated read-only and idempotent: drift_check (one action), drift_session (a batch, with per-action verdicts and a chain fingerprint that breaks if any earlier decision is rewritten or reordered) and drift_explain (the rules in order, with plain-language reasons). The mandate is a frozen dataclass, so an edit builds a new mandate instead of quietly widening the signed one; amounts are integer minor units; validity bounds are inclusive. Every rule was fired deliberately against the live endpoint - ALLOW within limits, then DENY amount, payee, audience, currency, window and intent from six separate probes, plus a three-action batch returning {submitted: 3, allowed: 1, denied: 2, breach_by_rule: {"amount": 1, "payee": 1}}. One footgun documented: an empty allowed_intents disables the intent rule and returned ALLOW for an intent named transfer_everything. Stated limits, from the vendor, are honest ones: it does not verify signatures (AP2's job), does not execute, keeps no state, and intent arrives as untrusted input from the agent; proving what actually happened is the same author's attest. Install trap, verified: the README says pip install drift, but PyPI drift is an unrelated CMS package at 0.0.7 and drift-mcp returns 404 - install from a clone with pip install -e .. Hosted free tier is 100 checks a day, then x402 per call on Base; self-hosting is free.

    • YouTube Kit MCP - Channel Analytics, Uploads and Comment Moderation · local stdio server uvx youtube-kit mcp plus the ytk CLI, from the youtube-kit 0.6.0 PyPI package (Python 3.12+, MIT, github.com/eukosh/youtube-kit created August 21, 2026, last push October 19, 2026, two open issues, no stars yet): the operator's own YouTube channel as an API - analytics totals and breakdowns by day, month, video, country, device, OS, traffic source, playback location, age, gender and subscriber status; videos (get, categories, resumable upload with progress, metadata update, set thumbnail, wait for processing, like or dislike, rating, delete); comments (list published, held for review or likely spam, replies, post, reply, edit, delete, approve, hold, reject, ban the author); playlists (list, get, items, create, update, image, add, remove, move, delete); channel (get, recent activity, logged-in channels, about info, banner, watermark, home-page sections); search across videos, channels and playlists; subscriptions. Multi-channel by design: one ytk auth login per channel and --my-channel / my_channel per call. The agent-safety surface is what earns the entry: one JSON document per command on stdout, a JSON error object with a named exit code on failure (2 bad input through 10 timeout), quota cost stated in every --help and every tool description, two-step deletes that require a second call naming the exact target, damage limits that refuse to delete a video with more than 100 views or a public video older than 7 days, and idempotent already_gone successes. Auth is your own Google Cloud project (YouTube Data API v3 plus YouTube Analytics API, Desktop OAuth client, roughly five minutes with ytk auth guide), which is deliberate: the 10,000-unit daily quota belongs to a project, not a shared client - reads 1 unit, search 100 per page of 50, most writes 50, guarded deletes 52, an upload 1,600. Not covered: captions, localizations, live streaming, memberships. Not affiliated with Google. Catalog gap closed: before this entry the only video-platform server in the catalog was tiktok-transcript-mcp; there was no YouTube channel operations entry at all.
    • PhilForms MCP - Philippine Government Forms Filled into Sealed PDFs · local stdio client npx -y github:philforms/philforms-mcp (Node 18+, no dependencies, MIT) in front of the PhilForms HTTPS API (https://philforms.com, OpenAPI 3.1, api version 1.0.0, live: openapi.json returns 200 and states 1,342 forms): search and fill official Philippine government forms across BIR, SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, GSIS, COA, CSC and GPPB with every input mapped to its printed box, so a TIN lands digit by digit in its cells. Five tools - search_forms, get_form_parameters (the fill contract: every parameter, label, type, format and choice), check_form_values (validate before filling, rendered as it would print), fill_form (PDF plus tamper-evident document id), verify_pdf - over a wider documented API with dossier, ingest, scan and extraction endpoints and a verification ledger. The design decision worth recording: a value the form cannot hold is refused with the reason instead of being coerced, so a workflow fails loudly at the check step rather than quietly printing a plausible wrong certificate. Pricing is published in PHP by the plans endpoint (/api/v1/plans, 200): a free watermarked tier that still issues clean first-of-pack forms plus 5 clean 2307s a quarter and 5 clean 2316s a year, 500 test fills on a pk_test_ key, credits where fill costs 1 and check, preview and verify cost 0 (revise 0 within 7 days, at most 5 edits), and form packs at 79 PHP for one form and 299 PHP for five, valid 12 months. The endpoint reported is_checkout_available: false at probe time, so the schedule is confirmed and the purchase path is not. Fills and prints; you file - not affiliated with any agency.

    • ACMP MCP - On-Prem IT Management with Approval Gate · self-hosted Streamable HTTP on your own ACMP server at http://<HOST>:8765/ (JSON-RPC 2.0, protocol 2025-06-18; one personal API key per operator, optionally bound to that person's real ACMP identity): the Aagon ACMP client and asset management platform exposed as 118 tools across ten areas - clients and inventory (OS, last logged-on user, hardware, offline machines, agent versions, low disk space), software and security (installed software and search, outdated software, missing and failed Windows updates, CVEs with score and last scan time, Defender health, BitLocker state, licence over- and under-deployment), jobs and execution (acmp_run_powershell as SYSTEM), client commands and kiosk writers (optional, off by default), containers, assets and master data including contracts expiring soon, 18 helpdesk tools (read, create, update, close, reopen, comment, work time, costs), and TeamViewer support links - plus acmp_call over all 167 Public API commands. The approval gate is the design centre: reads run immediately, a write freezes as a request showing the plain-text PowerShell, the requester and the target machine, and runs only after one named approver agrees; execute and delete need two different approvers. Approval happens in a browser outside the model, and approver tokens are independent of the API keys. MIT; requires ACMP 6.9/6.10 with AESB/SICS and the Public API on Windows Server with .NET Framework 4.8; documentation is in German. Repository github.com/Herzog-GmbH/acmp-mcp created October 11, 2026 with release mcpb-v1.0.0 (Claude Desktop extension) on October 18, 2026. Not probed by endpoint: the server runs behind the customer's own firewall, so there is no public URL to initialize against.

One new business-relevant entry, catalogued with a guide: a shared growth-experiment memory for teams and their agents.

    • Hypotize MCP - Growth Experiment Memory for Agents · hosted Streamable HTTP at https://api.hypotize.ai/mcp (OAuth 2.1; you sign in and choose what the agent may do): a shared experiment memory for teams and their agents - 21 tools over a project's tested backlog, framework-scored ideas (ICE, PIE, RICE or a custom framework), an enforced lifecycle with no skipped stages, and outcomes, evidence and learnings recorded together. Seven tools read the record (projects, project context and writing language, the backlog and pipeline, one experiment with its score and latest comments, learnings, tags and custom frameworks), twelve update it (create and update projects, import a backlog in all-or-nothing batches of 50, create ideas with variants, update experiments without overwriting newer work, record a vote and recalculate priority, transition stages, record the outcome with learning and evidence, add dated comments, set the action plan, create tags and frameworks) and two delete records, off until you grant the delete scope at connection. It keeps the record, not the test runner - Hypotize does not run A/B tests or assign traffic. Ships with three skills (growth experiments, weekly review, backlog import); works with Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, Kimi, OpenClaw, Hermes and any MCP client. Publisher: Hypotize (hypotize.ai; plugin repo github.com/viluca94/hypotize-plugin).     Integration with CorpusIQ¶

    CorpusIQ is the connector layer that lets AI assistants read the systems a business already runs on - accounting, payments, CRM, email, files and analytics - and answer with the source named. It is read-only by design: it retrieves data and never writes to, or acts in, a connected system, which is what makes it safe to point at live accounts.

    This page is part of the CorpusIQ directory, the reference we maintain for the MCP server and agent-skill ecosystem. Run alongside CorpusIQ, a third-party server like this one can be combined with a company's own business data in a single answer.
